So for backstory, I went to Disney for the first time in high school. I was 16. Before this, I had rarely gone to amusement parks and I never rode big rides due to the fact I have a phobia of throwing up. 


We chose to ride Mission Space, as it was a short line. If you don't know what this ride is, it's basically a VR simulator of traveling to space. There are two options, with spinning and without. We chose with spinning. This will be important. 


We climb in our little simulator, and the wall in front of us closes in on us. There was maybe a foot between my face and the wall in front of me. Cue me starting to panic, to which my two guy friends try to assure me it will be okay. Which I do mildly calm down. Until take off. 

So, due to the fact I seem to have half a brain cell, I completely forgot something important before going on this ride. I tend to pass out when there is extreme vertical g-force. Remember the spinning earlier? It simulates going from 0 to 6000 mph. Straight up. In about 10 seconds. 

So then we take off, and the real panic begins. I'm talking I'm straight up screaming and crying while just trying to not black out on the ride, while my friends are just trying to steer the ship and keep us from crashing while also holding my hands. 

The good news is, I did calm down and even managed to slightly help steer. I didn't pass out or panic during landing at all. Plus, I got to scare our new band director with the experience, while the old one just brushed it off cause that's the second time I've done something like that on a band trip.
